metaDescription: Six pressure washers under $1000: two Simpson gas units, cordless EGO, and Greenworks and Westinghouse electrics compared on PSI, GPM and pump type.
expertTake: The Simpson PowerShot 3500 with a Honda GX200 and 2.5 GPM is the best all-round buy, a gas machine whose engine and flow are both real. The Simpson 4400 PSI at 4.0 GPM is the choice for professional-speed concrete work. Skip gas altogether if you only wash a car and patio, because a 2000 rated PSI electric Westinghouse does that quietly. Check the live price and kit contents before ordering.
introParagraphs: A thousand-dollar ceiling covers every serious home use case, from a plug-in compact washer to a professional-flow gas unit. The trap is reading the largest number on the box, since peak pressure says little about how fast a machine cleans. Use rated figures wherever the listing gives them.

Pressure and flow work together, and the pump and engine behind them decide durability. Prices move and the $1000 cap reflects listing prices when this guide was updated, so check the live number before buying.

products.name: Simpson PowerShot 3500 PSI 2.5 GPM Honda GX200 Gas
products.description:
The PowerShot 3500 pairs a Honda GX200 engine with a 3500 PSI, 2.5 GPM pump. Multiplying the two gives about 8,750 cleaning units, which is the number that predicts how fast the machine strips grime. The Honda engine is a commercial-grade unit with a low-oil shutdown that protects it if you forget the dipstick.

A 25-foot Morflex high-pressure hose resists kinks and abrasion, which matters because hoses and quick-connect fittings are common failure points. Compared with the 4400 PSI Simpson, it has less flow but a smaller engine and a more manageable machine. Compared with the Greenworks electric, it cleans several times faster but needs fuel and noise tolerance.

Ownership is typical gas care: oil changes, stabilized fuel, air filter and winterizing the pump with antifreeze. Never run the pump dry, and wear hearing protection. Chock the wheels, keep the nozzle pointed down when you pull the starter, and let the hose fill with water before you start the engine so the pump never runs dry. Use the 25-degree tip for siding and the 15-degree tip for concrete.
products.bestFor: Homeowners who clean decks, drives and siding often and want real durability.

products.name: Simpson PowerShot 4400 PSI 4.0 GPM CRX 420cc Gas
products.description:
This is professional-class hardware: a 420cc engine drives an industrial triplex plunger pump to produce 4400 PSI at 4.0 GPM. That is roughly 17,600 cleaning units, double the cleaning rate of the 3500 PSI machine. Triplex pumps are the serviceable, long-lived pump type found on commercial equipment, unlike the sealed axial cam pumps of consumer units.

The tradeoff is size and demand: a 420cc engine is a roughly 14 to 15 horsepower class motor and the machine is heavy. A 4 GPM flow also needs a garden supply that can deliver it, otherwise the pump starves. Compared with the 3500 PSI model, it is faster on big concrete areas, and it is overkill for a car.

Expect to service the pump oil, keep the inlet screen clean and winterize with antifreeze. A machine this large is happiest when the water supply keeps up, so use a full-size hose and confirm your tap delivers at least the rated flow. A surface cleaner attachment turns it into a driveway-stripping machine.
products.bestFor: Large driveways, patios and contractor-style work.

products.name: Greenworks 3000 PSI 2.0 GPM Brushless Electric
products.description:
The Greenworks electric uses a 14 amp brushless motor and claims 3000 PSI with 2.0 GPM. A flow of 2.0 GPM is high for a household electric, and the maker says its JETTFLOW technology delivers up to 50 percent more flow, which helps reach higher areas. Brushless motors run cooler and quieter than brushed ones.

Compared with the Westinghouse electrics, it lists the highest flow. Compared with the gas Simpsons, it is far quieter and starts with a trigger, but it cleans at a fraction of their rate. Electric peak PSI is a maximum, not a sustained rating, so judge the machine by flow.

There is no fuel, no oil and almost no maintenance beyond draining the pump before freezing weather. Cold water cleaning is fine for most dirt, but grease needs detergent and patience. Coil the hose loosely and drain the pump after each use in cold weather. Store it where the cord is out of foot traffic.
products.bestFor: Quiet, low-maintenance cleaning of decks, siding and cars.
pros: 2.0 GPM is high for an electric

products.name: EGO POWER+ HPW3200 Cordless Pressure Washer
products.description:
EGO's HPW3200 combines two 56V ARC batteries in Peak Power mode to reach 3200 PSI, with ECO, High and Turbo modes. Being cordless, it can be used anywhere there is a garden hose or a water source, with no cord to drag or fuel to buy.

Battery energy limits runtime, particularly in Turbo, so it suits short jobs: cars, bikes, grills and patios. Compared with the Greenworks, it frees you from the outlet but costs more in batteries. Compared with the gas units, it is quiet and starts instantly.

Confirm whether the listing includes batteries and a charger. Short sessions suit it best, so plan the job and charge both packs beforehand. Use Turbo only for stubborn stains and drop to ECO for rinsing to stretch runtime. Confirm whether batteries and a charger are included before you buy.
products.bestFor: Short jobs without an outlet, for owners of the EGO platform.

products.name: Westinghouse WPX3000e 3000 Max PSI Electric
products.description:
Westinghouse is unusually candid: the WPX3000e lists 3000 max PSI and 1.76 max GPM but also 2600 rated PSI at 1.1 rated GPM. The rated pair is the sustained performance, around 2,860 cleaning units, and the max pair is a peak. A maintenance-free axial three-piston pump and a 25-foot abrasion resistant hose come with it.

That candor makes comparison easy. Against the Greenworks, the rated numbers are lower on flow. Against the compact ePX3500, it has more sustained pressure.

It is a straightforward electric for light to medium chores. Because the rated and max values differ, read the sticker on the machine rather than the marketing headline. Keep the soap nozzle for detergent and switch to a narrow tip for rinsing. Drain the pump before the first freeze.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want honest rated numbers in an electric.

products.name: Westinghouse ePX3500 2500 Max PSI Compact Electric
products.description:
The ePX3500 is a small, 19-pound electric with 2000 rated PSI at 1.2 GPM and a 20-ounce onboard soap tank. It stands 16.5 inches tall, so it fits in a closet.

It is the easiest to store and carry here. Compared with the WPX3000e it has less pressure. Compared with the gas units it is a fraction of the cleaning rate.

Good for cars, bikes and patio furniture. It fits in a closet and weighs only 19 pounds, so you will use it more often than a heavy machine. Fill the onboard soap tank sparingly and rinse the lines afterward. A garden hose of normal length is enough, because the flow demand is modest.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Cleaning units equal PSI times GPM. The Simpson 4400 PSI at 4.0 GPM makes about 17,600, the Simpson 3500 at 2.5 GPM makes about 8,750, and the Westinghouse WPX3000e rated pair makes about 2,860. Flow often sets cleaning speed more than the pressure headline. Use the formula on every listing to compare like with like.

The Westinghouse listings give max PSI and also the lower rated PSI at rated GPM. The rated pair is what the machine delivers while running. A label showing only a max number for an electric is a peak, not a sustained rating. Check the data plate on the machine when it arrives.

The 4400 PSI Simpson uses a triplex plunger pump, which is serviceable and long-lived. Consumer machines use axial cam pumps such as the Westinghouse axial three-piston pump, which are economical but usually not rebuildable. Ask whether the pump has a replaceable seal kit before you buy.

The Honda GX200 on the 3500 PSI Simpson is a commercial-grade engine with a low-oil shutdown. The 420cc CRX drives the 4 GPM pump. An engine must be sized for the pump, roughly 11 horsepower for 3000 PSI at 4 GPM. Check the oil-level sensor works at the first start.

Gas gives the most flow. Electric is quiet and low upkeep. Cordless, such as the EGO, is portable but battery-limited. Pick based on the surfaces and your tolerance for engine care. Add the battery cost for any cordless option.

Hoses and quick-connects fail first. The Simpson's 25-foot Morflex and the Westinghouse braided hoses resist kinks better than cheap ones. Check for metal fittings. Replace a cracked hose rather than taping it.

howToChoose.intro: Start with the surface, since concrete, wood and paint need very different settings.
Tiers are relative and show where extra spend buys flow and durability.

cards.label: Gas
cards.text: The two Simpson units give 2.5 and 4.0 GPM and clean concrete quickly. They are loud and need fuel and winterizing. They also tolerate long jobs.

cards.label: Electric
cards.text: The Greenworks and Westinghouse units are quiet and simple. They max near 2 GPM and clean slowly on big areas. They work well in apartments or garages.

howToChoose.note: Pick gas for big concrete; electric for light work. Many owners end up with one electric and one gas.

howToChoose.intro: Noise and neighbors matter more than most buyers expect.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: High GPM and a surface cleaner attachment so concrete cleans evenly. A surface cleaner attachment speeds a driveway job enormously.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: Both Simpson gas units fit best. The 3500 PSI model is the practical choice. Do the driveway in strips to avoid zebra stripes.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clean large areas often. The Simpson 4400 PSI is the next step. Triplex pumps also last longer.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You wash a car and furniture. The ePX3500 is enough. Spend the savings on detergent and a good extension hose.
